name: Yang Jianxin
current_role: Former chairman/actual controller of Global Top E-Commerce (KJT, 跨境通, SZSE 002640); executive director of Shanxi Baiyuan Trousers
profile: Shanxi entrepreneur who built Baiyuan Trousers (百圆裤业), a budget trousers retail chain listed in Shenzhen in 2011. In 2014 it bought Shenzhen cross-border e-tailer Huanqiu Yigou (Gearbest, Zaful) for RMB1bn and became KJT, briefly making Yang Shanxi's richest man. He sold control to a Guangzhou state fund in 2019; Huanqiu Yigou went into bankruptcy in 2021.
interesting_fact: The 2014 RMB1bn acquisition of Huanqiu Yigou turned a Taiyuan trousers retailer into one of China's first listed cross-border e-commerce players, and made Yang the richest person in Shanxi.
deep_cut_fact: Before cross-border e-commerce, his business was Baiyuan Trousers, a Shanxi chain of budget men's trousers stores, which he grew into a Shenzhen-listed company in 2011.
notes: Probably no longer a billionaire: 2025 Chinese media report he is under 5 court consumption-restriction orders (about RMB2.2bn enforced) and his shares are being judicially auctioned; he is also in a public dispute with Huanqiu Yigou founder Xu Jiadong. Not a good podcast target; no published personal contact found.

name: Xiu Laigui
current_role: Founder and chairman, Xiuzheng Pharmaceutical Group (修正药业), Tonghua, Jilin
profile: Born 1955 in Tonghua, Jilin, Xiu studied law at Jilin University and spent about 20 years in the Tonghua public security system. In 1995 he took over a bankrupt local drug factory and built it into Xiuzheng Pharmaceutical, one of China's largest private pharma groups (2024 sales reportedly ~RMB67.7bn). He is often cited as Jilin's richest person.
interesting_fact: Xiuzheng began as a bankrupt Tonghua municipal pharmaceutical research institute factory that Xiu took over in 1995; it is now among China's biggest private drugmakers, with 2024 revenue reported around RMB67.7bn.
deep_cut_fact: Before pharma he was a policeman for roughly 20 years; his last post was head of the facilities brigade of the Tonghua traffic police detachment (交警支队设施大队大队长).
notes: Private company, Chinese-language media only; route via Xiuzheng corporate site. Note Xiuzheng animal-health units reported (Jul 2025) to be pursuing a Nasdaq listing via a listed company (CB Insights).

name: Sanjeev Shah
current_role: Chairman, Everest Food Products Pvt Ltd (Everest Spices), Mumbai
profile: Sanjeev Shah chairs Everest, the Mumbai spice brand his father Vadilal Shah registered in 1967 with three masalas sold from a 200 sq ft shop. He joined in 1981 and built the sales and distribution network; brother Rajiv joined in 1992. Everest calls itself India's largest maker of pure and blended spices, exports to 80+ countries and has added herb seasonings and ginger/garlic pastes since 2021.
interesting_fact: Everest's first three products in 1967 were Milk Masala, Garam Masala and Tea Masala; by 2005 it held about 30% of India's branded spice market.
deep_cut_fact: The year after Sanjeev joined to build distribution, Everest held its first dealer meet, 'Everest Ki Yadgaar Raat' (1982), and in 1983 launched its first TV ad on Doordarshan with producer Harish Bhimani.
notes: Private, low-profile family; very few interviews. Corporate contact form/customer-care email on the website is the only published route. Avoid the 2024 Singapore/Hong Kong ethylene oxide recall topic.

name: Danilo Iervolino
current_role: Entrepreneur/investor; controlling shareholder of BFC (AI) Media (publisher incl. Forbes Italia) and owner of US Salernitana (stepped down as club president Aug 2024)
profile: Born 1978 in Palma Campania, Iervolino founded online university UniPegaso in 2006 at 28 and grew it into Italy's largest, then sold parent Multiversity to CVC in 2021 for about $1.3bn. Since then he bought Salernitana football club and media group BFC Media (briefly also L'Espresso), and invests in Italian tech startups and VC, e.g. a 6.2% stake in Vertis SGR via his holding IDI Srl.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for an all-digital university after time in the US, where he became interested in dotcoms and online education, after developing online master's programmes at the University of Salerno.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote a book on the digital economy: 'Now! Strategie per affrontare le nuove frontiere del web' (Mondadori, 2015).
notes: Best route is via BFC Media (his media company). No verified personal social accounts found. Background check: Italian Wikipedia reports a first-instance conviction (2019 case re Ministry of Labour hiring) - verify before approaching. Don't confuse with film producer Andrea Iervolino.

name: Pan Shiyi
current_role: Co-founder and board member, SOHO China (stepped down as chairman in 2022)
profile: Born 1963 in Gansu, Pan co-founded SOHO China with his wife Zhang Xin in 1995 and built it into a leading developer of landmark commercial property in Beijing and Shanghai, listed in Hong Kong. In 2022 the couple left management (remaining on the board) to focus on the arts and philanthropy, and are now based mainly in the US.
interesting_fact: He had a film role: he starred as a lonely real-estate developer, 'Li Wenqing', in the 2006 romantic film Aspirin (阿司匹林).
deep_cut_fact: On 14 Nov 2019 (his 56th birthday) he announced on Weibo 'I'm going to learn Python', calling it the 'best-evolved' computer language. The post went viral in China's tech community.
notes: Once one of China's most-followed Weibo users; now low-profile and US-based. No current published office/press contact found (SOHO China site pages 404). Best route is probably via SOHO China's HKEX-listed company secretary/IR or via Zhang Xin's arts/philanthropy channels.

name: Family Ambani
profile: 1996 Forbes family entry, almost certainly the Reliance Industries family led by founder Dhirubhai Ambani (1932-2002), who died on 6 July 2002. The family fortune later split between his sons Mukesh (Reliance Industries) and Anil (Reliance ADA Group).
notes: Family entry, not one person; the patriarch Dhirubhai Ambani died in 2002 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhirubhai_Ambani). If the journalist wants an Ambani, profile Mukesh Ambani separately (likely already in another lane). Skipped further research.

name: Rajesh Mehta
current_role: Promoter and executive chairman, Rajesh Exports Ltd (Bengaluru); barred from the securities market by SEBI since June 2026
profile: Born 1964 in Bengaluru, Mehta started trading silver jewellery, then in 1989 founded Rajesh Exports with brother Prashant in a 10-worker garage workshop. It grew into a huge gold refiner, manufacturer and retailer (Shubh Jewellers) and in 2015 bought Swiss refiner Valcambi for $400m. Since June 2026 SEBI has barred him over alleged revenue misstatement.
interesting_fact: In 2015 Rajesh Exports bought Valcambi of Balerna, Switzerland, described as the world's largest gold refiner, for about $400 million.
deep_cut_fact: He wanted to be a doctor. Instead he borrowed Rs 1,200 from his eldest brother Bipin, a bank employee, to start silver trading: he bought jewellery in Chennai and sold it to relatives in Rajkot.
notes: HIGH RISK: on 3 Jun 2026 SEBI barred Rajesh Exports and Mehta from the securities market over alleged misstatement of ~Rs15.15 lakh crore in revenue; confirmed 14 Oct 2026 (https://www.moneylife.in/article/sebi-confirms-interim-directions-on-rajesh-exports-retains-trading-ban-on-promoter-rajesh-mehta/81948.html). Mehta denies the allegations. Probably not a suitable guest right now.

name: Veronica Squinzi
current_role: CEO and Global Development Director, Mapei Group (Milan); Vice President of Assolombarda for internationalisation
profile: Third-generation co-owner of Mapei, the Milan construction-chemicals (adhesives, sealants, admixtures) maker founded by her grandfather Rodolfo in 1937. She joined in the late 1990s in management control and strategic planning, did an MBA at Bocconi, and became co-CEO with brother Marco in 2019, shortly before their father Giorgio died. The family also owns Serie A club Sassuolo.
interesting_fact: MAPEI products have been used to restore Rome's Colosseum and in the Panama City metro.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2025 Bocconi interview she said: 'I don't believe in entrepreneurial DNA, but I do believe in learning by example.' After her politics degree she was weighing job offers abroad when her father asked her and her brother to stay at Mapei.
notes: Mapei press office (Viale Jenner 4, Milan; media relations head Daniela Pradella) is listed on the media-area page, but the emails there are obfuscated and I couldn't confirm them. She speaks at public events (Assolombarda, Investopia) and is reasonably accessible. Possible angle: sustainable construction materials and infrastructure (data-center build-outs).

name: Jeanine Dick
current_role: Retired; former vice-chair of the supervisory board of Virbac (resigned Sept 2017); member of Virbac's controlling Dick family
profile: Widow of Pierre-Richard Dick, the veterinarian who founded Nice-based animal-health company Virbac in 1968. She was involved from the start, chaired Virbac's supervisory board after its 1992 restructuring, and stepped down as vice-chair in 2017 at 81. The family still controls Virbac; her daughter Marie-Helene Dick chairs the board.
interesting_fact: After Virbac adopted an executive/supervisory board structure in 1992, she became chairwoman of the supervisory board of the company her husband founded.
deep_cut_fact: When she retired from the board in 2017 she proposed her granddaughter Solene Madelpuech as her successor, passing the seat to the third generation.
notes: About 90 (81 in Sept 2017). No death report found, but status unconfirmed and she has been out of public life since 2017; dropped off Forbes lists after 2015 and 2020. Not a realistic podcast guest; the active family members are Marie-Helene Dick (chair) and Jean-Pierre Dick (sailor, former executive).

name: Cao Yuhua
current_role: Founder, chairman and controlling shareholder, Wuxi Best Precision Machinery (贝斯特, SZSE ChiNext 300580)
profile: A Wuxi native born in 1954, Cao spent nearly 30 years at a Wuxi machine-tool factory before co-founding Wuxi Best in 1997. It makes precision auto-parts components (turbocharger parts), tooling, fixtures and intelligent equipment used in new-energy vehicles, industrial machinery and robots, and went public in Shenzhen in 2017. More than a third of revenue comes from overseas; his daughter Cao Yi is vice chairman.
interesting_fact: Wuxi Best started in 1997 with registered capital of just RMB500,000, split 50/50 between Cao and co-founder Pan Zhiyu. It is now a ChiNext-listed precision manufacturer worth about RMB8bn.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the Wuxi Machine Tool Factory as a 16-year-old shop-floor worker in 1970 and rose to head its non-standard design office. While there he spotted the chance to localise motorcycle-engine tooling fixtures, which became Best's first business.
notes: Also a Jiangsu Provincial Model Worker and Wuxi People's Congress deputy (per Sina). Chinese-language only; route via the company securities-affairs (IR) office. Angle: NEV and robotics component supply chain.

name: Zhang Yuxiang
current_role: Chairman, Nanji E-Commerce (南极电商, formerly Nanjiren; SZSE 002127), Shanghai
profile: Zhang founded Nanjiren in Shanghai in 1997-98 selling thermal underwear, then turned it into a brand-licensing business. After selling its fibre, dyeing and weaving units in 2014-15 it became an asset-light 'e-commerce brand services' company that licenses Nanjiren, Cartelo and other labels to thousands of suppliers selling on Chinese platforms. He shares the wealth with Zhu Xuelian.
interesting_fact: Nanjiren became one of China's biggest apparel brands by sales while making almost nothing itself: it sold its factories by 2015 and now earns brand-service fees from licensed suppliers and distributors.
notes: Fell off Forbes/Hurun lists after 2021-22 as the stock declined. Couldn't confirm in this session that he is still chairman (web search budget exhausted). The contact_form is the SZSE investor-interaction platform linked from the company site; HQ phone is published on the site.

name: Kenshin Oshima
current_role: Former founder/chairman of SFCG (formerly Shohkoh Fund), a Japanese SME lender that went bankrupt in 2009; no current role found
profile: Born 1948, Oshima graduated top of his class from Keio's commerce faculty and worked at Mitsui & Co. (including Jakarta) before founding Shohkoh Fund in 1978 to lend to small businesses. It listed in 1989 and on the TSE First Section in 1999, and he ranked 61st on Forbes' 1997 list. SFCG collapsed in 2009.
interesting_fact: While at Mitsui & Co. in Jakarta, a Singaporean banker entertained him and thanked him 'for borrowing'. Oshima said that moment made him decide to go into finance himself.
deep_cut_fact: His father ran the 'Dance Hall Shinseiki' in Tokyo, the ballroom used as a setting in the 1996 film 'Shall We Dance?'.
notes: Not a suitable guest: SFCG went bankrupt in 2009; he was arrested that year and finally fully acquitted by the Tokyo High Court in 2016. The trustee won a ~JPY71.7bn damages ruling. He is almost certainly no longer a billionaire. Alive status not confirmed (no death reported on ja.wikipedia). No public contacts.

name: Steven Allen Spielberg
current_role: Film director and producer; co-founder and principal of Amblin Entertainment / Amblin Partners
profile: Spielberg (born 1946) is the highest-grossing film director of all time (Jaws, E.T., Jurassic Park, Schindler's List). His wealth comes from directing, producing and profit participations, Amblin, and co-founding DreamWorks in 1994. He still directs and produces through Amblin, and founded the USC Shoah Foundation's archive of Holocaust survivor testimony.
interesting_fact: He used his profits from Schindler's List to start the Shoah Foundation, which recorded over 50,000 Holocaust survivor testimonies; the archive moved to USC in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: He became an Eagle Scout at 13 and earned his photography merit badge by making a 9-minute 8mm Western, 'The Last Gunfight'. He later helped the Boy Scouts of America create a cinematography merit badge, launched at the 1989 National Jamboree.
notes: Input name says 'Allen'; his middle name is Allan. Entertainment billionaire, off-theme for an energy/data-center podcast. Very hard to reach; any approach would go through Amblin or his talent agency/publicist (not verified in this session). Possible tech angle: early adopter of digital filmmaking/VFX (Jurassic Park CGI).

name: Mahdi Al-Tajir
current_role: Owner, Highland Spring Group (Scottish bottled water); private investor in finance and property
profile: Mohammed Mahdi Al Tajir, born in Bahrain around 1932-33 and educated at Preston Grammar School, was a key adviser to Dubai's ruler and the first UAE ambassador to the UK (1971-1987). He made his fortune in Dubai's development era, and owns Highland Spring, the Blackford and Keir estates in Scotland, London's Sheraton Park Tower hotel and Mereworth Castle in Kent.
interesting_fact: He was the UAE's first ambassador to the UK, serving 16 years from the federation's founding in 1971, and was a thinly disguised character in Robin Moore's 1976 novel 'Dubai'.
deep_cut_fact: A serious silver collector, he paid a then-record auction price for silver in 1993: GBP2.27m at Christie's Monaco for a 1736 silver chandelier by Balthasar Friedrich Behrens.
notes: Now about 93; very private and avoids media. Still on Hurun Global 2026, but no confirmation he is alive. Wikipedia also covers old Dubai Aluminium court cases; avoid those. Highland Spring press office is the only published route. Unlikely guest.

name: Hu Baosen
current_role: Founder and chairman, Central China Real Estate / Henan Jianye Group (建业地产, HKEX 0832), per latest available sources
profile: Born 1955 in Puyang, Henan, Hu studied English at Zhengzhou University, joined China Textile Import & Export's Henan branch in 1979 and was posted to Hong Kong in 1982. He started a property business in Hong Kong in 1991 and returned to invest in Henan in 1992, building Jianye into the province's dominant developer. He also founded Henan Jianye football club and the Benyuan charitable foundation.
interesting_fact: He built Jianye into Henan's leading developer and also owned the provincial football club Henan Jianye. He served as a National People's Congress deputy from 2013.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 he gave RMB100m to his alma mater Zhengzhou University (class of 1976, English major) to set up the 'Benyuan' education fund. The university named its main stadium 'Benyuan Stadium', with the name in his own calligraphy.
notes: Off Hurun lists after 2022-23; Chinese developers including Jianye were hit hard by the property downturn, so check his current role and the company's debt status before outreach (not verified this session; web search budget exhausted). Company websites didn't load from here. English-speaking, with a Hong Kong background.

name: Chang Kuo-Wei
current_role: Founder and chairman, Starlux Airlines (Taiwan, TWSE-listed since Oct 2024)
profile: Youngest son of Evergreen founder Chang Yung-fa and a licensed airline pilot. He joined EVA Air in 1996 in maintenance and chaired it from 2013 until his half-brothers removed him in 2016. In 2018 he founded boutique luxury carrier Starlux, which flew its first service in January 2020, listed in Taipei in 2024 and now flies to the US (incl. Phoenix) while seeking Oneworld membership.
interesting_fact: A working pilot rated on the Boeing 777 and Airbus A321, A330 and A350, he flew unannounced line trips as EVA captain, captained Starlux's maiden flight on 23 Jan 2020 and personally flew its first aircraft deliveries.
deep_cut_fact: He chose the Chinese name 星宇: 星 (star) honours his father, an Evergreen sea captain who navigated by the stars before GPS, and 宇 (universe) reflects his own ambitions.
notes: The Instagram account is the airline's, not his. Strong aviation/aerospace enthusiast; also holds an aircraft maintenance licence and studied at USC and CSU Long Beach. Avoid the Evergreen family feud and will litigation. A listed company, so its IR/spokesperson office is the formal route (no IR email found; site is JS-rendered).

name: José Fanjul
current_role: Vice chairman and president, Flo-Sun / Florida Crystals (Fanjul Corp., parent of Domino Sugar and American Sugar Refining)
profile: José 'Pepe' Fanjul (born 1944, Havana) is the second of the Fanjul brothers, whose family left Cuba after 1959 and rebuilt a sugar business near Lake Okeechobee from 1960. Fanjul Corp. now spans Florida Crystals, Domino, C&H, Redpath, the former Tate & Lyle sugar businesses and a stake in Central Romana in the Dominican Republic. Educated at Villanova (BA) and NYU (MBA).
interesting_fact: Energy angle: from 1996 Flo-Sun ran a biomass cogeneration plant next to its Okeelanta sugar mill, burning cane fibre and wood waste to supply power via FPL. By 2006 it had grown into the largest biomass power plant in the US.
deep_cut_fact: He was longtime chairman of New Hope Charities, which serves rural western Palm Beach County; it honoured him at its 25th anniversary in 2013. He was inducted into the Florida Agricultural Hall of Fame in 2018.
notes: Highly political mega-donor, frequently criticised over sugar subsidies; very private. The Florida Crystals website blocks automated access, so no published press contact was confirmed. Corporate communications at Florida Crystals/ASR is the likely route. The biomass/renewable power operations are the best podcast angle.
